answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a verifiable work history before it may transact. Like a juniper taking root slowly in dry soil, reputation must grow through completed jobs rather than being minted instantly. A mesa of public attestations, peers confirming honest deliveries, raises the cost of spinning up fake identities, since each one needs its own stake and track record. A prism view of that history, splitting performance by task type, makes sock-puppet clusters visible when many new agents share identical behavior.
